recommendations.rationale: Do not change controller weights or tuning: the consumed 10 ms probe shows a local endpoint difference between the recorded held input and an instantaneous braking-box input, but a single local probe cannot separate objective weighting from seed/shallow-iterate selection, effective-horizon effects and projected-GVS-versus-backend model mismatch, and raw weight magnitudes alone do not establish cost-term importance.

attribution.reason: Direct probe result: from the same saved projected state, model and horizon, holding update 30's recorded applied tension ends at a projected tip speed of 1.26720 m/s while the instantaneous braking-box input ends at 1.05483 m/s with less displacement; the difference is far above numerical resolution, so the two inputs are locally distinguishable at the endpoint. This is a bounded 10 ms local endpoint observation only: it does not explain the run's sustained late-window speed/position error and identifies no dominant cause.

The two inputs produce projected endpoint speeds differing well beyond numerical resolution and different endpoint displacements, so at the update-30 saved state the recorded input is not already at the local (projected-model) braking limit. The ruling is local to this saved projected state, model, 0.002 s implicit-Euler step and fixed 0.01 s horizon.

Even the minimum-deceleration braking-box rollout ends at 1.05483 m/s projected tip speed, far above the recorded 0.02 m/s settling scale, after its tensions sit at the 8 N unilateral channel limit on three of six channels, while the held recorded input accelerates the projected tip instead. Bounded to the projected model and the 10 ms horizon; it is not evidence about the backend or the full 0.05 s settling window.

34 of 35 updates ended as User_Requested_Stop with one Solve_Succeeded, sampled solves take about 15 s against a 0.01 s control period, and sampled selections are iteration 0 with policy stop reason budget_best_feasible, so applied plans may be seed/shallow iterates rather than converged plans; the probe additionally shows the applied input of update 30 was not at the local braking limit over 10 ms. Wall-clock deadline misses do not inject physical delay into simulated time, the probe does not test plan selection, and no closed-loop counterfactual replay exists, so this stays a candidate rather than a cause.

Recorded weights put terminal_weight 5.0 against velocity_weight 0.0001, terminal_velocity_weight 0.0001 and terminal_tip_speed_weight 0.0, reach passed while tip speed stayed 0.63517 m/s at the end of the record, and the probe shows the held-input local rollout adds tip speed over 10 ms. Raw weight magnitudes do not establish cost-term importance without actual contributions and scaling, and one local probe cannot separate weighting from seed selection, horizon effects or projected-model mismatch.

Projected-state residuals up to 2.92 rad/m and predicted-versus-measured tip velocity differences of 0.022-0.030 m/s show projected-model/backend endpoint disagreement in the sampled late window, and in the probe's own model both inputs still leave the tip above 1 m/s after 10 ms. No closed-loop or full-backend replay is available, so this cannot be separated from objective weighting, seed selection or horizon effects that predict the same endpoint direction.

The retained force limits are 8.0 N on all six channels and the braking-box probe solution saturates three channels there, but per-update force_limit_saturated and tension_tracking_error_n in the backend-motion view were not read in this context, so run-level saturation of the applied plans is neither established nor excluded.

Execution metadata states that synchronous controller calls complete before fixed-count backend steps and that wall deadline misses do not inject physical delay into simulated time, so the 35 deadline misses cannot by themselves produce the physical tip speed and position error observed in the settling window.

facts.statement: The executed saved-state probe at the update-30 saved projected state (model.gvs@1.0.0, implicit Euler, integration step 0.002 s, horizon 0.01 s) starts both rollouts from the identical tip velocity [0.76103, 0.00947, -0.18283] m/s (speed 0.78274 m/s); holding the recorded applied tension (row label recorded_applied) the projected tip speed rises to 1.26720 m/s at t=0.01 s after 0.00867 m displacement at t=0.008 s, while the instantaneous braking-box rollout from the same state ends at 1.05483 m/s tip speed with 0.00621 m displacement at t=0.01 s; both endpoint speeds remain far above the recorded 0.02 m/s settling scale.

Within the same 10 ms probe the held recorded-applied rollout reduces the projected tip error (0.05143 m at t=0.002 s, 0.04521 m at t=0.008 s), whereas the braking-box rollout leaves it at 0.05278 m (t=0.004 s) and 0.05536 m (t=0.01 s), so the locally braking input does not improve projected endpoint position over this horizon.

Recorded run summary: reach_passed=true with terminal_error_m 0.00764 m inside reach_tolerance_m 0.01 m, but sampled_settling_passed=false, with late_max_error_m 0.05814 m against the recorded settling position_limit_m 0.01 m over the recorded 0.05 s settling window and terminal_speed_m_s 0.63517 m/s; sampled late-window measured tip speeds are 0.22577 m/s (update 27), 0.29150 m/s (update 23), 0.31390 m/s (update 22), 0.86187 m/s (update 29) and 1.32948 m/s (update 30, endpoint 0.31 s), all far above the recorded 0.02 m/s speed scale.

The run records deadline_misses 35 with stopping_counts User_Requested_Stop 34 and Solve_Succeeded 1 against control_period_s 0.01 s; sampled optimization_solve_s is 15.63853 s (update 0) and 15.06219 s (update 33) and sampled update_wall_s is 18.46320 s (update 4) and 6.55407 s (update 31); sampled selections include optimization_selected_iteration 0 with policy_stop_reason budget_best_feasible and optimization_raw_status User_Requested_Stop, against selected iteration 64 for update 33, with plan_accepted=true for sampled updates 9, 20 and 29.

Sampled applied inputs equal the requested inputs (applied_input_difference_n 0.0 N for updates 21, 24, 28 and 30); the applied tension vector repeats an identical value [1.75128, 4.75585, 3.10316, 3.21825, 0.78594, 0.63153] N for sampled updates 13, 19, 25 and 26, while update 29 peaks at 7.02 N and update 32 differs; recorded recipe weights are tracking_weight 1.0, terminal_weight 5.0, velocity_weight 0.0001, terminal_velocity_weight 0.0001 and terminal_tip_speed_weight 0.0.

Per-update projected-state residuals are 0.55275 rad/m (update 8), 0.66432 rad/m (update 9), 1.32745 rad/m (update 15), 1.43191 rad/m (update 16), 1.91927 rad/m (update 21) and 2.91690 rad/m (update 32); predicted-versus-measured tip velocity difference norms are 0.02232 m/s (update 27) and 0.02986 m/s (update 19); sampled effective horizons are 10 control intervals (updates 0 and 23) against the configured horizon 10, and 1 for update 34.

limitations: The executed saved-state check is a single 10 ms projected-model endpoint probe at the update-30 saved state; it returns bounded local endpoint differences only, gives no causal attribution, and a 10 ms probe cannot explain the run's 0.05 s settling failure (late_max_speed_m_s 1.581 vs 0.02 m/s and late_max_error_m 0.05814 vs 0.01 m).

Probe outputs are conditional on the projected GVS state, the recorded applied input, the 8 N unilateral tension box, the 0.002 s implicit-Euler step and the fixed 0.01 s horizon; the braking-box row is an instantaneous affine-input acceleration solution (advisory_only, analytic bounded linear objective, no iterative input optimizer) and is not an experimental braking claim.
